nodes.label: Render to Vercel + Artifact Migration
nodes.rationale: The dashboard is being moved off Render onto Vercel serverless plus a self-contained claude.ai Artifact. render.yaml, *.bat, README.md and .env.example Render references are to be removed and vercel.json / api/index.js becomes the only serverless target.

nodes.label: Scheduled Cloud Agent Routine (trig_015V5Hc7BXCBFWbWzrehdVsa)
nodes.rationale: Work is split by capability: the scheduled agent does repo-only prep in ONE PR, while Vercel deploy and Artifact publishing stay human because the cloud agent has no Vercel auth and publishing needs an interactive session. If publish-clean is not on origin when it runs it falls back to origin/dashboard-cloud or origin/main and its PR needs rebasing.

nodes.label: Self-contained Artifact Dashboard (artifact/dashboard.html)
nodes.rationale: A static, self-contained copy of the dashboard that can be published as a claude.ai Artifact and re-published on every change; publishing requires an interactive session so it is human-owned.

nodes.label: Repoint ESP32 Cloud Upload URL
nodes.rationale: The ESP32 POSTs to a hardcoded cloud host, so the device upload URL/DNS must be moved to the Vercel deployment and verified before the Render service is deleted.

nodes.label: PC Vehicle Health Dashboard
nodes.rationale: The ESP32 keeps doing CAN monitoring and SD logging; the PC-hosted Node server owns the customer-facing UI and proxies the logger so the browser never hits the ESP32 directly (avoids CORS and gives one local address).

nodes.label: Customer Login via Supabase Auth
nodes.rationale: The Node server calls supabase.auth.signInWithPassword with an anon-key client rather than exposing Supabase to the browser, so the access token never leaves the server-managed cookie.

nodes.label: Stateless Encrypted __Host- Session Cookie
nodes.rationale: The Supabase session is encrypted with a key derived from SESSION_COOKIE_SECRET and stored in an httpOnly __Host- cookie, so there is no server-side session store. This keeps the server stateless and horizontally deployable (Render/Vercel serverless) at the cost of cookie size and no server-side revocation.

nodes.label: Self Sign-up and Device Claiming
nodes.rationale: POST /api/auth/signup uses the anon-key client so Supabase sends the confirmation email and no session is returned. POST /api/devices/claim runs on the service-role client, matches devices.device_id + devices.claim_code, requires a device_status_latest row (proof the device really reported) and inserts user_devices idempotently; it is throttled per-IP and per-user to resist claim-code guessing.

nodes.label: DASHBOARD_AUTH=off Trusted-LAN Bypass
nodes.rationale: Setting DASHBOARD_AUTH=off skips login and device claiming entirely. Documented as trusted-LAN only because it removes all per-user isolation, so it must never be used on the public cloud deployment.

nodes.label: Cloud Mode (DASHBOARD_MODE=cloud)
nodes.rationale: A hosted server cannot reach canlogger.local on the customer's LAN, so the data direction is inverted: the ESP32 pushes vehicle-health summaries up to the public server instead of the server polling the device.

nodes.label: POST /api/cloud/status Upload Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Authenticated by DEVICE_UPLOAD_TOKEN rather than a user session, since the ESP32 has no login. The token is stored only as a sha256 upload_token_hash on the devices row.

nodes.label: Local Logger API Proxy (GET /api/status, /api/files, /view, /download)
nodes.rationale: The PC server proxies these four ESP32 endpoints so the browser talks to one local origin: avoids CORS and hides the changing ESP32 address/IP from the UI.

nodes.label: Service Mode (Raw CAN Log Gating)
nodes.rationale: Raw CAN logs are hidden unless Service mode is enabled, so ordinary customers see only friendly event reports; the raw frames are technician-only detail.

nodes.label: Offline Fallback Demo Data
nodes.rationale: If the logger is powered off the dashboard still opens and shows demo-style fallback data with an offline message, so a dead device never produces a broken/blank UI during a demo.

nodes.label: Future GPS / Location Fields
nodes.rationale: Optional GPS status, last known location, lat/long, event location and trip route fields are carried through the data model ahead of the hardware; the Location page deliberately shows 'GPS not connected' until a GPS module is added.

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres Schema for CAN Logger Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Supabase Auth for login plus Row Level Security for per-user isolation. Migrations are applied in filename order; schema.sql and seed.demo.sql are the superseded pre-Supabase model kept only for history.

nodes.label: Row Level Security Model
nodes.rationale: All six tables have RLS enabled plus force row level security. authenticated users get SELECT only: profiles/user_devices restricted to (select auth.uid()), devices and telemetry restricted to devices listed in the user's user_devices. No insert/update/delete policies for authenticated on telemetry — only the service role writes, and it bypasses RLS. The server additionally filters reads by user_id/device_id as defense in depth.

nodes.label: Service-Role-Only Write Path
nodes.rationale: user_devices has no INSERT RLS policy at all; only the server's service-role path writes it. This means a compromised user token cannot grant itself access to another device, at the cost of the server holding the service-role key.

nodes.label: profiles Table
nodes.rationale: One row per auth.users id, auto-created by the handle_new_user trigger. Holds display name plus customer code.

nodes.label: devices Table
nodes.rationale: ESP32 CAN logger devices. upload_token_hash is the sha256 of DEVICE_UPLOAD_TOKEN so the plaintext token is never stored; claim_code is the shared secret a customer types to claim the device.

nodes.label: user_devices Table
nodes.rationale: Join table deciding which auth user can view/service which device with roles viewer/service/owner. Written only by the server's service-role path — no INSERT RLS policy exists.

nodes.label: device_status_latest Table
nodes.rationale: Upserted latest vehicle-health snapshot per device — one row per device rather than an append log, so the Home page reads a single row. Its existence also proves a device has reported, which device claiming requires.

nodes.label: device_events Table
nodes.rationale: Append-only alert/event history per device, capped by the retention trigger.

nodes.label: report_files Table
nodes.rationale: Metadata for downloadable report / log files surfaced on the Reports page.

nodes.label: device_events Retention Trigger (0003)
nodes.rationale: An AFTER INSERT trigger caps device_events at 500 rows per device, bounding unbounded growth from a chatty logger on a free-tier Postgres. Renumbered from 0002 to keep repo and cloud migration history in step.

nodes.label: handle_new_user() RPC Lockdown (0002)
nodes.rationale: Revokes EXECUTE on handle_new_user() from the API roles because it is trigger-only; leaving it callable over PostgREST would let a client forge profile rows. Already applied on the cloud project and backfilled into the repo so the two histories match.

nodes.label: Device Claiming Migration (0004 devices.claim_code)
nodes.rationale: Adds devices.claim_code plus a partial index for self-service claiming; deliberately makes no RLS change because the claim path runs as service role anyway.

nodes.label: App Wiring Flow (signup, login, claim, request, upload)
nodes.rationale: Five distinct client identities by purpose: anon-key client for signup/login, service-role client for claiming and ESP32 ingestion, and a per-request client carrying the user's access token so RLS applies to normal reads.

nodes.label: Per-Request Access-Token Client
nodes.rationale: Each request builds a Supabase client with that user's access token so RLS is enforced by Postgres, and reads still filter explicitly by user_id/device_id as defense in depth against a policy mistake.

nodes.label: Dashboard SPA Shell (index.html)
nodes.rationale: Single static HTML shell: all five pages are pre-rendered as sections toggled by the .active class and data-page nav buttons, with /app.js loaded as a module. No framework and no client-side router.

nodes.label: Login / Sign-up Screen (#loginScreen)
nodes.rationale: One form serves both sign-in and sign-up via the #authToggle button and a shared #authSubmit, avoiding a separate signup route in the UI.

nodes.label: Connect Your Device Screen (#claimScreen)
nodes.rationale: Shown to a signed-in account with no devices. Collects Device ID and claim code and tells the customer the device must have powered on and sent at least one cloud update, mirroring the server's device_status_latest precondition.

nodes.label: Home Page (#homePage)
nodes.rationale: Health band plus metric panels (monitoring status, vehicle state, latest event, logger connection) and live signal readouts for speed, brake pressure, acceleration and events.

nodes.label: Alerts Page (#alertsPage)
nodes.rationale: Customer-friendly alert cards; service detail is explicitly hidden unless service mode is enabled.

nodes.label: Reports Page (#reportsPage)
nodes.rationale: Session summary metrics plus an Available Files list backed by the logger file endpoints and downloadable health reports.

nodes.label: Settings Page (#settingsPage)
nodes.rationale: Logger profile form (address, device name, optional token, service-mode toggle) with a Test connection action and inline troubleshooting checklist duplicating the README guidance.

nodes.label: Location Page (#locationPage)
nodes.rationale: Placeholder map and GPS metric panels that state 'GPS not connected' / 'Ready', reserving the layout for a future GPS module rather than hiding the page.

nodes.label: Connect Your Logger Setup Banner (#setupBanner)
nodes.rationale: First-run nudge telling the user to enter canlogger.local or the ESP32 IP in Settings, jumping straight to the Settings page.

nodes.label: Render Web Service can-logger-dashboard
nodes.rationale: Node runtime web service with buildCommand npm install and startCommand npm start — the same server.js entrypoint as local mode, differing only by environment variables. Secrets (DEVICE_UPLOAD_TOKEN, DASHBOARD_AUTH_PASSWORD, DATABASE_URL) use sync:false so they are set in the Render dashboard, never committed.

nodes.label: DEVICE_UPLOAD_TOKEN Secret Env Var (render.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Marked sync:false so the value lives only in the Render dashboard. Its sha256 is what the devices table stores as upload_token_hash.
